owner_posts.post_text: In a world that moves fast, yoga reminds us to slow down, breathe, and reconnect with ourselves.

A patient came to us after nearly three months of continuous fever following a knee replacement surgery. During this period, she had consulted multiple doctors across cities and was treated for common infections like typhoid, malaria and dengue. Despite repeated tests and treatments, the fever persisted, along with joint pain, mouth ulcers and extreme fatigue — without a clear diagnosis.

At SRV Hospitals, under the care of Dr. Avilash Tiwari @dr.avilash_tiwari, the approach shifted from treating symptoms to understanding the full cause. A structured evaluation for long-standing fever was initiated, looking beyond routine infections and considering inflammatory and immune-related conditions.

Advanced testing revealed two key findings. One was a mild, uncommon form of leptospirosis that does not present with the typical severe symptoms and often goes unnoticed. More importantly, investigations confirmed an autoimmune condition called Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE), where the immune system becomes overactive and causes ongoing inflammation — leading to persistent fever and joint symptoms.

featured_reviews.name: Rax Rav
featured_reviews.review_text:
You said:

This hospital operates under charitable funding, yet arbitrary and unfair practices are openly carried out here. Recently, when I tried to click photos for writing a review, the security guard forced me to delete them. The most shocking part is that the staff themselves take patients’ mobile phones and write reviews on their behalf.

The behavior and treatment given to patients here is extremely poor. Although the services and facilities are funded by government money and taxpayers like me, the attitude towards patients is very disrespectful.

There is a lot of favoritism and unfair practices, especially for X-ray and other ground floor services. Known persons are given priority numbers, and in some cases, people are asked for unofficial payments (“tea money”) to move ahead in the queue.

Earlier, when I directly complained to the management about an eye doctor, only then did I receive proper service. On 6th February, I was again forced to approach the management and submit a written application for my patient’s treatment (attached).

For the past three years, I have been visiting this hospital for various treatments and services. Medicines are often prescribed unnecessarily. In the female ward, since many patients do not raise complaints, nurses behave carelessly and sometimes rudely. They do not properly monitor medication schedules, and if questioned, they respond with threats or arguments. Due to such behavior, I had to take my patient home.

The security guards and staff are extremely rude and arrogant. Each time, I have had to control the situation by warning them that I would file complaints with the management.

Fake and manipulated reviews are being written in bulk by making patients stand in line and write them.

Overall, this is a very poorly managed hospital with unsatisfactory services and inexperienced doctors.
